$comment: Generated by facts/validate.mjs. Do not edit by hand; run `npm run facts`.

mars-constants.description: Planet-wide constants for Mars, plus the two solar-system constants the derived solar-flux records need (sun.*, astro.*). Values from the NASA NSSDCA Mars Fact Sheet unless noted; atmospheric composition from Curiosity SAM.

jezero-environment.description: Surface environment at Jezero crater, the Mars Sandbox v0.1 region. Primary source is Perseverance MEDA. Values marked approx need to be re-derived from the PDS MEDA archive by the coding agent (see AGENT_BRIEF.md task F2).

mars-resources-isru.description: What has actually been demonstrated or measured for living off the land on Mars: oxygen production, regolith chemistry, agriculture trials. Engineering tier = demonstrated performance, not a fact about Mars.

mars.time.sol.label: Length of a sol (mean solar day)

mars.orbit.obliquity.label: Axial tilt (obliquity to orbit)
mars.orbit.obliquity.notes: Drives Earth-like seasons. Note obliquity has varied widely over Myr timescales (not relevant to gameplay).

mars.orbit.eccentricity.label: Orbital eccentricity
mars.orbit.eccentricity.notes: Large enough that solar flux varies ~45% between perihelion (southern summer) and aphelion.

sun.solar_constant_1au.label: Total solar irradiance at 1 au (solar constant)

uncertainty.note: the IAU 2015 nominal value is exact by definition; +/-0.5 is the uncertainty of the measured solar-cycle-23 mean it was rounded from

sun.solar_constant_1au.instrument: SORCE/TIM (solar-cycle-23 mean), adopted as the IAU 2015 nominal S_N
sun.solar_constant_1au.notes: Prsa et al. 2016 state the measured cycle-23 mean as 1361 +/- 0.5 W/m^2 and that IAU 2015 Resolution B3 adopts the rounded value as the nominal solar constant. The underlying measurement paper (Kopp & Lean 2011, GRL 38, L01706) is cited there but was not reachable when this record was written, so it is not listed as a source here.

astro.au.label: Astronomical unit

uncertainty.note: conventional unit of length, exact by definition (IAU 2012 Resolution B2)

astro.au.notes: Defined, not measured; recorded so the solar-flux formulas can reference the Sun-Mars distance ratio by id instead of quoting 1.5237 au as a bare literal. The primary document is IAU 2012 Resolution B2; its text is quoted in Prsa et al. 2016, which is what was verified.

mars.solar.constant_mean.label: Top-of-atmosphere solar irradiance at mean distance
mars.solar.constant_mean.notes: Perihelion ~713 W/m^2, aphelion ~490 W/m^2. Surface irradiance is further reduced by dust (see jezero.dust.optical_depth_typical).

mars.atmosphere.co2_fraction.label: CO2 volume mixing ratio (near surface)
mars.atmosphere.co2_fraction.notes: Measured at Gale; atmosphere is well mixed so applies globally at the surface.

mars.atmosphere.n2_fraction.label: N2 volume mixing ratio
mars.atmosphere.n2_fraction.notes: Relevant to any nitrogen-fixation or buffer-gas ISRU design.

mars.atmosphere.mean_molar_mass.label: Mean molar mass of air
mars.atmosphere.mean_molar_mass.formula: sum(x_i * M_i) over CO2, Ar, N2, O2
mars.atmosphere.mean_molar_mass.notes: Needed for air density: rho = p*M/(R*T). At 700 Pa and 210 K this gives ~0.017 kg/m^3.

mars.radiation.gcr_dose_equivalent_surfa.label: GCR dose equivalent rate at the surface (Gale, solar max)
mars.radiation.gcr_dose_equivalent_surfa.notes: Measured near solar cycle 24 maximum when GCR flux is low; expect up to ~2x at solar minimum. Gale is -4.4 km MOLA, so has more atmospheric shielding than Jezero (~-2.5 km); Jezero dose will be slightly higher. Absorbed dose rate 0.210 +/- 0.040 mGy/day.

mars.radiation.gcr_dose_equivalent_cruis.label: GCR dose equivalent rate in transit (inside MSL spacecraft)

mars.interior.heat_flow_mean_plesa2016.label: Mean present-day surface heat flux (thermal evolution models)
mars.interior.heat_flow_mean_plesa2016.notes: No direct measurement exists: the InSight HP3 probe failed to reach depth. Earth's mean is ~90 mW/m^2. Geothermal power is not viable; subsurface thermal stability is.

mars.interior.heat_flow_mean_frizzell202.label: Mean crustal heat flow (geochemistry + InSight crustal thickness)
mars.interior.heat_flow_mean_frizzell202.notes: Largest uncertainty is crustal thickness, not chemistry. Treat heat flow as 3 to 27 mW/m^2 until measured.

jezero.location.landing_site.label: Perseverance landing site (Octavia E. Butler Landing)
jezero.location.landing_site.notes: Jezero is a ~50 km crater on the NW rim of the Isidis basin; Noachian lake basin with a fluvial delta.

uncertainty.note: approx; re-derive from MOLA MEGDR 128 ppd at the landing coordinates

jezero.terrain.dem_source.label: Terrain data products for the v0.1 region
jezero.terrain.dem_source.value: MOLA MEGDR 128 ppd (global, ~463 m/px) + HiRISE 1 m/px stereo DTM over the Perseverance field site
jezero.terrain.dem_source.notes: Stack et al. 2020 mapped the field site at 1:5000 on a 25 cm/px HiRISE orthomosaic and 1 m/px DTM. Use that DTM for the playable region; MOLA for the crater-scale context.

jezero.pressure.first_reading.label: Surface pressure, first MEDA report (sol 1, Ls~6)

jezero.pressure.annual_envelope.label: Surface pressure envelope over a Mars year

uncertainty.note: approx envelope; driven by the seasonal CO2 polar-cap cycle (~±8%) plus a diurnal thermal-tide cycle of a few percent

jezero.pressure.annual_envelope.notes: APPROX. Agent task F2: replace with min/max/mean from the PDS MEDA PS archive for MY36.

jezero.temperature.air_annual_mean.label: Mean near-surface air temperature over a Mars year (1.45 m)
jezero.temperature.air_annual_mean.notes: Reported as 'around minus 55 degrees Celsius' averaged across seasons.

jezero.temperature.air_diurnal_max_typic.label: Typical afternoon maximum air temperature
jezero.temperature.air_diurnal_max_typic.notes: APPROX. Ground (not air) temperature at midday can approach or exceed 273 K in summer; the ground-air difference is large on Mars because the air is so thin. Agent task F2.

jezero.temperature.diurnal_range_typical.label: Typical day-night air temperature swing
jezero.temperature.diurnal_range_typical.notes: This swing, not the mean, is what kills unheated structures. A thermal-mass design must bridge it every sol.

jezero.surface.thermal_inertia_range.label: Surface thermal inertia along the traverse
jezero.surface.thermal_inertia_range.notes: Low values = loose dust/sand (fast heating and cooling); high = bedrock. Matters for regolith-as-insulation designs.

uncertainty.note: varies with illumination angle; minimum near noon

jezero.dust.optical_depth_typical.label: Typical visible dust optical depth (clear season)

uncertainty.note: approx; Jezero was reported clearer than Gale at landing

jezero.dust.optical_depth_typical.notes: APPROX. Surface irradiance ≈ TOA * exp(-tau/cos(sza)) * (scattering correction). Agent task F2: pull the Mastcam-Z tau series.

jezero.dust.optical_depth_storm_jan2022.label: Peak visible optical depth, regional dust storm 5-11 Jan 2022 (Ls 153-156)
jezero.dust.optical_depth_storm_jan2022.notes: A regional storm roughly quarters usable solar power for days. Global storms (2018 killed Opportunity) can reach tau ~8-10 and last months; none has been measured at Jezero yet.

jezero.dust.dust_devil_frequency.label: Dust devil frequency of occurrence (first 365 sols)
jezero.dust.dust_devil_frequency.notes: Peak 12:00-13:00 LTST. Dust devils at Jezero can exceed 100 m diameter. A dust devil damaged a MEDA wind sensor in the Jan 2022 storm. Relevant to solar panel dust loading (also cleaning events).

jezero.radiation.gcr_dose_equivalent_est.label: Estimated GCR dose equivalent at Jezero

uncertainty.note: scaled from Gale measurement for ~1.9 km less atmospheric shielding and solar-cycle variation

jezero.radiation.gcr_dose_equivalent_est.notes: Rule of thumb: ~1 m of regolith or ~2-3 m of water reduces GCR dose substantially; shielding is a design parameter, not a fact. Agent: model, do not state as measured.

jezero.subsurface.shallow_ice_likelihood.label: Likelihood of accessible water ice in the top 5 m at Jezero latitude (18 N)
jezero.subsurface.shallow_ice_likelihood.notes: SWIM maps show consistent shallow ice mostly poleward of ~35-40 deg latitude. Jezero is a science site, not a resource site. Water for a Jezero base is therefore hydrated minerals, atmospheric extraction, or import. This is a design constraint the agent must surface.

jezero.subsurface.deep_liquid_water.label: Liquid water in fractured mid-crust (global inference from InSight)

uncertainty.note: single-site seismic inversion; authors argue it is likely global

jezero.subsurface.deep_liquid_water.notes: Volume exceeds proposed ancient oceans. Not accessible with any plausible drilling; relevant to astrobiology scenarios, not to base water supply.

jezero.subsurface.thermal_stability_dept.label: Depth below which diurnal temperature swing is negligible

uncertainty.note: depends on thermal inertia; the annual wave penetrates several metres

jezero.subsurface.thermal_stability_dept.formula: skin depth d = sqrt(2*kappa/omega), kappa from thermal inertia and regolith density
jezero.subsurface.thermal_stability_dept.notes: Agent must compute this from the primitives library, not hard-code it. Buried or regolith-covered structures see the mean (~218 K), not the swing.

isru.moxie.o2_rate_peak.label: MOXIE peak oxygen production rate
isru.moxie.o2_rate_peak.instrument: Perseverance MOXIE (solid oxide electrolysis of CO2)
isru.moxie.o2_rate_peak.notes: At >=98% purity. Design goal was 6-10 g/h. Power-limited by a 4 A supply; the instrument draws roughly 300 W during a run. Use for scaling: a crew of 4 needs ~3.3 kg O2/day; NASA's full-scale concept targets 2-3 kg/h.

isru.moxie.o2_total.label: Total oxygen produced over the MOXIE campaign (16 runs)
isru.moxie.o2_total.notes: First run sol 60 (20 Apr 2021) produced 5.4 g in ~1 h at 751 Pa, 201 K ambient.

regolith.perchlorate.phoenix_site.label: Perchlorate content of soil at the Phoenix site (68 N)

uncertainty.note: 'a few tenths of a percent' in all three samples; WCL leachate ~2.4 mM ClO4-

regolith.perchlorate.global_presence.label: Perchlorate is present globally in Martian regolith
regolith.perchlorate.global_presence.notes: Detected by Phoenix (WCL) and inferred from Curiosity SAM evolved-gas chlorine releases at Gale. Toxic to humans (thyroid) at these levels; must be removed or the regolith must not be used for food crops. Remediation (washing, microbial perchlorate reduction) is a scenario assumption, not a demonstrated capability.

agriculture.simulant_trials.wageningen_2.label: Crop growth in NASA JSC-1A Mars regolith simulant (Earth greenhouse)
agriculture.simulant_trials.wageningen_2.value: 9 of 10 crops produced edible biomass comparable to Earth potting soil control; spinach failed; radish, rye, cress produced viable seed
agriculture.simulant_trials.wageningen_2.notes: IMPORTANT CAVEATS the agent must carry into any model: (1) JSC-1A contains no perchlorate; (2) grown under Earth gravity, pressure, light and CO2; (3) simulant was amended with organic matter. This supports 'regolith can be a substrate', not 'Mars soil grows food'. Crop yield under Mars light (~43% of Earth TOA, further cut by dust) is an open modeling question.

water.shallow_ice.midlatitude_depth.label: Depth to shallow ice where SWIM finds it consistent (northern mid-latitudes)

uncertainty.note: SWIM distinguishes <5 m and >5 m zones; depth is site-dependent

water.shallow_ice.midlatitude_depth.notes: Candidate human landing regions (Arcadia, Utopia, Deuteronilus) are chosen for this. If the product adds a second region, pick one of these so water ISRU becomes a real design space.

atmosphere.water_vapor.extraction_viabil.label: Atmospheric water column

uncertainty.note: strong seasonal and latitudinal variation; MCD provides columns

atmosphere.water_vapor.extraction_viabil.notes: Extracting water from Mars air means processing ~10^5 m^3 of air per litre. Technically possible, energetically terrible. Any module claiming atmospheric water harvest must show the energy budget.

nssdc-mars-factsheet.citation: NASA NSSDCA Planetary Fact Sheet: Mars. D. R. Williams, NASA GSFC. Last updated 19 May 2025.

jpl-mars-at-a-glance.citation: JPL InSight press kit, "Mars at a glance" (sol length 24 h 39 m 35 s; atmosphere 95.3% CO2, 2.7% N2, 1.6% Ar by the older Viking numbers).

sam-mahaffy-2013.citation: Mahaffy, P. R. et al. (2013). Abundance and isotopic composition of gases in the martian atmosphere from the Curiosity rover. *Science* 341(6143), 263-266. doi:10.1126/science.1237966

meda-2023-naturegeo.citation: Rodriguez-Manfredi, J. A. et al. (2023). The diverse meteorology of Jezero crater over the first 250 sols of Perseverance on Mars. *Nature Geoscience*. doi:10.1038/s41561-022-01084-0

meda-year1-upvehu-2023.citation: University of the Basque Country / UPV-EHU press release on the first Mars year of MEDA results (Sánchez-Lavega, Hueso, del Río-Gaztelurrutia, Munguira), Jan 2023. Mean air temperature ~-55 °C, large diurnal swings, seasonal pressure cycle, Jan 2022 dust storm.

meda-first-report-2021.citation: NASA/JPL first MEDA weather report, Feb 2021: surface pressure 718 Pa, clearer atmosphere than Gale at landing. Press reports:

meda-rds-epsc2026.citation: Rodriguez-Veloso, R. et al. (2026). Aerosol optical properties and dust deposition as observed by MEDA RDS at Jezero crater. EPSC 2026, EPSC2026-378. Also EPSC2024-508 and EPSC-DPS2025-680 by the same group.

lemmon-2022-duststorm.citation: Lemmon, M. T. et al. (2022). Dust, sand and winds within an active Martian storm in Jezero crater. *Geophysical Research Letters* 49(17). Peak tau ~2 over 5-11 Jan 2022.

meda-dustdevils-rds.citation: Toledo, D. et al. Dust devil frequency of occurrence and radiative effects at Jezero crater, Mars, as measured by MEDA RDS. 374 dust devils in the first 365 sols; peak 12:00-13:00 LTST.

meda-pds-archive.citation: PDS Atmospheres Node, Mars 2020 MEDA bundle (pressure, temperature, wind, humidity, RDS, TIRS per sol).

rad-hassler-2013.citation: Hassler, D. M. et al. (2013). Mars' surface radiation environment measured with the Mars Science Laboratory's Curiosity rover. *Science* 342(6169). GCR dose equivalent 0.64±0.12 mSv/day (some outlets report 0.67 after re-averaging); absorbed dose 0.210±0.040 mGy/day; cruise 1.84±0.30 mSv/day.

rad-dlr-2016.citation: Reitz, G. et al. (2016). Radiation measurements of MSL-RAD on the surface of Mars. ICES 2016. Confirms 0.64±0.12 mSv/day surface, 1.84±0.3 cruise.

plesa-2016-heatflux.citation: Plesa, A.-C. et al. (2016). How large are present-day heat flux variations across the surface of Mars? *JGR Planets*. doi:10.1002/2016JE005126. Average 23.2-27.3 mW/m²; InSight site 18.8-24.2.

frizzell-2023-heatflow.citation: Frizzell, K. R., Ojha, L., Karunatillake, S. (2023). Bounding the unknowns of martian crustal heat flow from a synthesis of regional geochemistry and InSight mission data. *Icarus* 405. doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2023.115700. Mean crustal heat flow 3.0-13.9 mW/m².

wright-2024-midcrust-water.citation: Wright, V., Morzfeld, M., Manga, M. (2024). Liquid water in the Martian mid-crust. *PNAS*. doi:10.1073/pnas.2409983121. Water-saturated fractured igneous rock at 11.5-20 km best explains InSight seismic data.

hecht-2009-perchlorate.citation: Hecht, M. H. et al. (2009). Detection of perchlorate and the soluble chemistry of martian soil at the Phoenix lander site. *Science* 325(5936), 64-67. doi:10.1126/science.1172466

kounaves-2010-wcl.citation: Kounaves, S. P. et al. (2010). Wet Chemistry experiments on the 2007 Phoenix Mars Scout Lander mission: Data analysis and results. *JGR* 115, E00E10. doi:10.1029/2009JE003424

swim-psi.citation: Subsurface Water Ice Mapping (SWIM) project, Planetary Science Institute / JPL (Putzig, Morgan et al.). SWIM 1.0 (2019, northern hemisphere), 2.0 (2020, southern + Tharsis), SWIM4IMIM (ongoing, CTX/HiRISE).

mola-megdr.citation: Smith, D. E., Neumann, G. A. et al. MGS MOLA Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record (MEGDR), MGS-M-MOLA-5-MEGDR-L3-V1.0, NASA PDS Geosciences Node, 2003. 4 to 128 pixels/degree topography relative to the areoid.

stack-2020-jezero-map.citation: Stack, K. M. et al. (2020). Photogeologic map of the Perseverance rover field site in Jezero crater constructed by the Mars 2020 science team. *Space Science Reviews* 216:127. doi:10.1007/s11214-020-00739-x. Mapped at 1:5000 on a 25 cm/px HiRISE orthomosaic and 1 m/px HiRISE stereo DTM. Now open access (CC-BY 4.0 since July 2025).

mcd-lmd.citation: Millour, E., Forget, F. et al. The Mars Climate Database, version 6.1 (2022-2024). LMD/IPSL, Open University, Oxford, IAA; ESA/CNES supported. Global circulation model outputs: pressure, temperature, winds, dust, water vapour and ice columns, radiative fluxes, several dust scenarios (climatology, cold, warm, storm). Free on request; web interface for quick looks.

moxie-hoffman-2022.citation: Hoffman, J. A. et al. (2022). Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment (MOXIE): Preparing for human Mars exploration. *Science Advances* 8(35). doi:10.1126/sciadv.abp8636. Seven 2021 runs, ~50 g total, 6-8 g/h; first run 5.4 g at 751 Pa / 201 K.

moxie-nasa-final-2023.citation: NASA, Sept 2023: MOXIE completes 16th and final run; 122 g total; peak 12 g/h at >=98% purity, twice the original goal; full-scale concept 2-3 kg/h.

moxie-mit-2021.citation: MIT News, 21 Apr 2021: MOXIE first oxygen, 5.4 g in one hour; power supply limits to 12 g/h.

wamelink-2019-crops.citation: Wamelink, G. W. W. et al. (2019). Crop growth and viability of seeds on Mars and Moon soil simulants. *Open Agriculture* 4(1). doi:10.1515/opag-2019-0051. Ten crops in NASA JSC-1A Mars simulant vs Moon simulant vs Earth potting soil; Mars simulant comparable to Earth control; spinach failed; radish, rye, cress seeds viable.

prsa-2016-iau-b3.citation: Prša, A., Harmanec, P., Torres, G., Mamajek, E. et al. (2016). Nominal values for selected solar and planetary quantities: IAU 2015 Resolution B3. *Astronomical Journal* 152(2), 41. doi:10.3847/0004-6256/152/2/41. The paper reproduces the resolution: nominal solar constant S_N = 1361 W/m^2 (exact), nominal solar luminosity 3.828e26 W; the measured solar-cycle-23 mean it was rounded from is given as 1361 +/- 0.5 W/m^2. It also quotes IAU 2012 Resolution B2: the astronomical unit is 149 597 870 700 m exactly.

nasa-dra5.citation: Drake, B. G. (ed.) (2009). Human Exploration of Mars Design Reference Architecture 5.0. NASA/SP-2009-566, plus Addendum NASA/SP-2009-566-ADD (July 2009). Six crew, three consecutive opportunities, ~500-day surface stays, pre-deployed cargo, ISRU for ascent propellant, nuclear surface power baseline, detailed mass and power budgets.

zubrin-mars-direct.citation: Zubrin, R. M. & Baker, D. A. (1990/1991). Mars Direct: A proposal for the rapid exploration and colonization of the Red Planet. Also Zubrin & Wagner, *The Case for Mars* (1996; rev. 2011), Free Press, ISBN 978-0684827575.

spacex-musk-2017-2018.citation: Musk, E. (2017). Making Humans a Multi-Planetary Species. *New Space* 5(2). doi:10.1089/space.2017.29009.emu. And Musk, E. (2018). Making Life Multi-Planetary. *New Space* 6(1). doi:10.1089/space.2018.29013.emu.

weinersmith-city-on-mars.citation: Weinersmith, K. & Weinersmith, Z. (2023). *A City on Mars: Can We Settle Space, Should We Settle Space, and Have We Really Thought This Through?* Penguin Press, ISBN 9781984881724. Hugo Award 2024; Royal Society Trivedi Science Book Prize 2024.

insight-hp3-2018.citation: Spohn, T. et al. (2018). The Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package (HP3) for the InSight mission. *Space Science Reviews* 214:96.

pds-general.citation: NASA Planetary Data System: https://pds.nasa.gov/ (Geosciences node for MOLA/HiRISE DTMs; Atmospheres node for MEDA, REMS; Imaging node for HiRISE/CTX).
